items.b: LAOPU GOLD'S FIRST-HALF PROFIT ROSE 88.18%, AND THE DIVIDEND TAKES THREE-QUARTERS OF IT
items.t: Recognised revenue was 19.808 billion yuan, up 60.3%. The larger 22.779 billion yuan figure circulating as revenue is sales performance, 13.04% higher. Profit attributable was 4.267 billion yuan. Basic earnings 24.16 yuan a share against an 18.02 yuan interim dividend, a 74.59% payout.

items.b: MOVADO'S SALES ROSE 4.9%, THE EXACT FIGURE BY WHICH FOSSIL'S FELL
items.t: The quarter to 31 July put net sales at $169.8 million and net income at $12.3 million against $3.0 million, or 4.10 times. Licensed brands grew 9.0% and owned brands 0.7%. Gross profit carried $3.2 million of IEEPA duty refunds. Fossil's quarter ended twenty-seven days earlier.

items.b: PLATINUM'S HELD MARK BROKE AFTER SEVEN SESSIONS AT $1,881.00
items.t: The carried figure sat $19.00 above the whole Kitco day range of $1,815.00 to $1,862.00. Rewritten to $1,816.00 on Kitco and CNBC agreeing within 0.202%, with TradingEconomics' $1,833.90 disclosed as a 0.986% divergence. Gold fell 0.926% to $4,579.50, silver 0.721% to $68.056.

items.b: DELHI'S CUSTOMS CHIEF HEARD EIGHT GRIEVANCES IN MUMBAI AND ASKED FOR A FLOW CHART
items.t: The Finance Minister nominated Manish Kumar to meet the trade at GJEPC's head office on 24 August. Rough valuation, 100% checking at Mumbai, RMS underuse and misdeclaration proceedings led the list. No relief, figure or timeline was published.

items.b: TEN CHINESE GOLD COUNTERS PRICED WITHIN SEVEN YUAN OF EACH OTHER
items.t: On 25 August the brand boards read 1,403 to 1,410 yuan a gram, a spread of 0.499%. Chow Sang Sang added 18 yuan in a session, or 1.295%. The 26 August pullback reached this desk single-source and is not printed.

items.b: PALLADIUM HELD AN EIGHTH SESSION AT $1,336.00, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS DELIBERATE
items.t: Kitco bid $1,294.00 against a $1,341.00 ask, TradingEconomics $1,309.00, CNBC $1,310.99. No two pages agree inside the band. Unlike platinum, the held mark still sits inside today's $1,292.00 to $1,364.00 day range, so it was carried rather than rewritten.

tape_ts: 27 Aug 2026, 06:01 ET - Kitco, corroborated on TradingEconomics and CNBC - Editor re-read at press time and wrote back gold at $4,579.50, silver at $68.056 and platinum at $1,816.00. Platinum's seven-session hold at $1,881.00 ended because that mark had drifted $19.00 above the whole day range; TradingEconomics' $1,833.90 diverges 0.986% and is disclosed. Palladium held an eighth session at $1,336.00, still inside its day range
